messaging_map.master_narrative: Carson Poore Consulting is one strategist in Indianapolis who plans the work and then builds it. For years the site said 'marketing agency'; the truth is simpler and bigger: a growth consultancy with four practices — marketing, technical, strategy, and coaching — for local businesses, founders, and nonprofits across central Indiana, and anywhere for the technical and coaching work. The model is the message: prices published on the site ($1,200, $2,400, or $4,800 a month, a $3,000 one-time strategy engagement, a reduced nonprofit rate), eight clients total, three months minimum then month to month, and you keep everything — your site, your Google profile, your ad accounts — if you leave. Indianapolis agencies have moved upmarket, AI shops can't do brand, and fractional CMOs hand you a plan without hands; Carson sits in the intersection none of them occupy, runs every engagement through five plain-English steps (Conviction, Your people, A sharp offer, The experience, Word of mouth), and talks like the candid friend who happens to be a strategist: he'll tell you what not to buy, when you're too early, and exactly what a month of work gets you.

practice_oneliner.marketing: Brand, campaigns, content, and email that make the right people notice you and talk about you — measured in calls, customers, and booked work, not impressions.
practice_oneliner.technical: The builds most marketing people can't do — AI agents and automation, websites and web apps, GoHighLevel and CRM, Google Ads, GA4 — practical, human-in-the-loop, and priced for small businesses.
practice_oneliner.strategy: A $3,000, one-time engagement: your positioning, your people, a sharp offer, and a 90-day plan you could run without me — the answer to 'what should we do first?'
practice_oneliner.coaching: A fractional CMO for owners and founders at $1,200–$4,800 a month — under the $5,000–$15,000 the category charges, with the plan and the hands in one person.

icp_messages.local_smb: Word of mouth built your business; it just stopped scaling. When Indianapolis searches for what you do, you'll show up — and every call, text, and form gets answered in minutes. Published prices, three months then month to month, monthly reports that count calls and booked jobs, and you keep everything if you ever leave. I'll also tell you what not to buy — starting with ads you're not ready for.
icp_messages.founders: You built the thing; now we get it to people. Start with the $3,000 strategy engagement — positioning, who it's actually for, a first repeatable channel — then keep me on as a fractional CMO at well under category rates. I think like an owner, own outcomes instead of deliverables, and build the automation too. If you're pre-product-market fit, I'll say so and send you off with homework instead of a retainer.
icp_messages.nonprofits: You're wearing five hats and marketing falls to whoever has ten spare minutes. Start with a free Ad Grant checkup — Google offers verified nonprofits $10,000 a month in free ads, and most orgs use about $300 of it — then one donor list everyone trusts, stories people understand, and numbers your board can read. The nonprofit rate isn't charity: the budgets are smaller and the work matters. A capacity-building grant may even cover it.

differentiators: Published pricing on the site — 12 of 13 competitors reviewed make you book a call to hear a number.
Eight clients, total: a person, not a pod — the structural opposite of the 6,000-brand outsourced-CMO volume model.

One person, four practices: the strategist who writes the plan also builds the automation, the site, and the ad account. Indy agencies don't build, AI shops don't do brand, fractional CMOs don't implement — the intersection is empty.
Actually in Indianapolis: the local SERP is held by out-of-state template farms; real neighborhoods, real local clients, one exact NAP everywhere.
Five plain-English steps, deliberately untrademarked — the candid counter to Growth Gears®, BRAVE™, and the framework soup.
Candor as policy: what not to buy, when you're too early, and 'three months minimum, because real change takes that long' instead of fake no-contract promises.
You keep everything if you leave — site, Google Business Profile, ad accounts, data — which pre-answers the burn stories this market carries.
Five ungated, instantly-scored free tools (no email, no login) that double as working proof of the technical practice.

risks: CLAUDE.md creative-batch rule applies to the five tools: build 2-3 (recommend Check-Up, Can Indianapolis Find You?, and the budget calculator) plus all five copy decks first and wait for approval before building the full batch.

The 36-file budget is spent exactly: email-marketing service page, the 'how to vet a marketing company' article, the GA4-diagnostic article, GoHighLevel-for-home-services article, and dedicated Carmel/Fishers suburb pages were deliberately deferred to phase 2 — adding any page now requires cutting another. No thin per-suburb doorway pages at launch; one towns-served block instead.

/services/coaching must never use 'business coach' language or compete on that SERP — Indy Chamber's free BOI coaching and ActionCOACH own it and anchor the price at free. Always 'fractional CMO / marketing advisor.'

Stat hygiene: never publish the single-source figures ($5.7B fractional market, $26B workflow-automation market, the 61%-no-ROI/$28K AI stat as numbers, vendor Indy CPC claims); attribute the $8,650 managed-Ad-Grant average as industry-reported; every on-page statistic needs its named source inline.

Do not chase head terms in titles: bare 'fractional CMO', 'gohighlevel expert', and 'web design indianapolis' are marketplace/incumbent SERPs — the question-format articles carry the national ranking load while service pages convert.

Proof gap: no named founder case studies exist yet — the founders pathway and /work must bridge honestly from local/nonprofit results ('industry data + my local results, named') rather than invent startup numbers; fabricated proof reads instantly as agency-speak to this audience.

Nav: 'Who I help' has no hub page, so its top-level link must point to a real anchor (/#who-i-help) and dropdowns must be keyboard-accessible with a no-JS fallback; verify Vercel cleanUrls serves services.html and services/*.html side by side (it does by default) and keep all 9 legacy paths byte-identical so no redirects are needed.

Site-level files ship with the build but don't count against 36: /llms.txt (H1 + blockquote summary + linked sections), robots.txt explicitly allowing GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot/ClaudeBot/Claude-SearchBot/PerplexityBot/Google-Extended/Bingbot, sitemap.xml with real lastmod (exclude /ticket and 404), Organization/ProfessionalService @graph with @id referenced on every page, visible 'Last updated' lines, and canonical URLs in one exact format.

Off-site work is load-bearing and lags 60-90 days: Bing Webmaster Tools + Google Search Console verification, GBP + Bing Places with identical NAP, free directory profiles (Clutch, GoodFirms, BrightLocal, ClearlyRated, Semrush Agency Partners), review-velocity system, and killing any listing that still says 'marketing agency' — ChatGPT can't cite pages Bing hasn't indexed, and ~6.5x of AI citations come via third parties.

Copy QA: run the 24-gate humanize checklist (commit as docs/copy-qa-checklist.md) on every page before ship — negative parallelism, banned vocab (which overlaps the brand ban list), triad stacking, 'whether you're X or Y', vague attribution, and uniform rhythm are the likeliest failure modes of generated copy; metas above are written to 140-160 chars and titles to ~60, so re-verify lengths after any edit; every page needs at least two of: a real price, the 8-client cap, the 3-month minimum, an Indy place name, a named method step.
